stories.headline: KOSYGIN IS ARRIVING HERE TODAY; MEETS 2 HOURS WITH DE GAULLE; ASSEMBLY TO OPEN THIS MORNING; MANY LEADERS DUE Mideast Session May Get Record Turnout of High Officials
stories.summary: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin is arriving in New York, meeting with French President Charles de Gaulle, as the United Nations Assembly is set to open with a record turnout of high officials, during the Cold War

stories.headline: RULING GENERALS REPORTED READY TO QUIT IN SAIGON; Ky and Thieu, in a Struggle Over Presidential Race, Offer to Step Down JUNTA WOULD KEEP REIN Successors Are Designated  Bitter Closed Meetings Enter Second Day Ky and Thieu Reported Ready to Step Down After 2-Year Rule
stories.summary: South Vietnamese leaders Nguyen Cao Ky and Nguyen Van Thieu are reportedly willing to step down as part of a power struggle, as the Vietnam War continues

stories.headline: JOHNSON EFFORTS TO MEET KOSYGIN APPEAR STALLED; But Some Russians Indicate Premier Is Eager to Hold Meeting in New York U.S. GESTURE IS SOUGHT Soviet President Visits Tito on Way to Conference in Cairo With Nasser Johnson Efforts to See Kosygin Seem Stalled, but Premier Is Said to Want Talks U.S. AIDES DISCERN LACK OF INTEREST Russians, on Other Hand, Say Soviet Leader Is Eager to Meet With President
stories.summary: President Lyndon B. Johnson's efforts to meet with Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin appear stalled, but some Russians indicate Kosygin is eager to hold a meeting in New York, as the Cold War intensified

stories.headline: LEADERSHIP POSTS AT STAKE IN VOTE; Tuesday Primary Also Will Decide 5 Judicial Races
stories.summary: A primary election in the Bronx will decide leadership posts and judicial races, with candidates like W Martinez and N Lugo competing

rounds.blurb: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin arrived in New York, meeting with French President Charles de Gaulle. The United Nations Assembly opened with a record turnout of high officials amidst the Cold War. South Vietnamese leaders Nguyen Cao Ky and Nguyen Van Thieu considered stepping down.

stories.headline: WRECKAGE VIEWED; Naval Survey Will Be Limited to Interests of Government; TWO OTHER INQUIRIES; Department of Commerce Will Study Cause of Accident to the HindenBurg; REICH GROUP ON WAY HERE; Sabotage Theory Discarded --Passenger and Officer Succumb to Injuries
stories.summary: The German airship Hindenburg crashed, and while sabotage is a possibility, it has been largely discarded as a cause, with the Department of Commerce set to study the accident

stories.headline: CABINET IN SESSION; All German Navy Craft Wait With Steam Up for Instructions LONDON MEETING CALLED Non - Intervention Group to Consider Safety Measures for Warships Off Spain SPANISH LINER IS SUNK Vessel With Heavy Passenger List Is Torpedoed by Rebel Submarine Off Barcelona "Measures" Not Divulged TEXT OF COMMUNIQUE SPANISH BOMBING STIRS THE REICH Serious Crisis for Reich Demand on London Likely News of Bombing Delayed Ambassador Davies Visits Parents' Home in Wales European Action Demanded Valencia Officials Silent Battleship Reaches Gibraltar Rebels Torpedo a Liner
stories.summary: A Spanish liner was torpedoed by a rebel submarine off Barcelona, and the German Navy is on high alert, as the Non-Intervention Group considers safety measures for warships off Spain

stories.headline: YOUNGSTOWN STEEL MILLS WILL CLOSE, IF MEN STRIKE, UNTIL THEY ASK JOBS BACK; SEEK A 'SHOWDOWN' Two Independents Plan to End Threat of Closed Shop Now UNION IS NOT ASKING ONE But Republic and Youngstown Sheet and Tube Bar Contract as Opening Wedge DISCRIMINATION CHARGED S. W. O. C. Asserts Union Men Suffer Lay-Offs--Walkout Is Held 'Inevitable' Day's Strike Developments Talk of Steel Shutdown 33,000 in Youngstown 2 STEEL COMPANIES PLAN 'SHOWDOWN' Conditions Held Different Prepared for Strike Discrimination Charged 'PEACE OR WAR' IN VOTE S. W. O. C. Leaders Stress Issue in Jones & Laughlin Ballot
stories.summary: Youngstown steel mills are set to close if workers strike, as Republic and Youngstown Sheet and Tube companies seek to end the threat of a closed shop, with the union charging discrimination against its members

stories.headline: ROYAL TITLE DENIED TO WINDSOR'S BRIDE; King Orders That Mrs. Warfield Shall Not Be Styled as 'Her Royal Highness' VICTORIA SET PRECEDENT Ministers Gave 'Advice' in the Recognition of Status to Duke, but Excluding His Wife Emphasis on Word "Only" ROYAL TITLE DENIED TO WINDSOR'S BRIDE Victory for Court Group Ministerial Responsibility Vagueness on Old Document Act Will Stop Speculation EDWARD ANGERED BY NEWS Refuses to Accept Defeat as Final, Associate Reports DUKE RE-ENGAGES DRIVER Reported to Have Phoned Him to Serve on Wedding Trip
stories.summary: King Edward has denied his bride, Wallis Warfield, the title of 'Her Royal Highness', following precedent set by Queen Victoria, in a decision that has angered the Duke of Windsor

rounds.blurb: The Hindenburg crashed, with sabotage largely discarded as a cause. The Department of Commerce studied the accident, while the German Navy waited for instructions. A Spanish liner was torpedoed by a rebel submarine off Barcelona.

stories.headline: 19-HOUR CONCERT ENDS BETHEL FAIR; Producer Says Town Has Asked Festival to Return
stories.summary: A 19-hour concert featuring Jimi Hendrix and Sha-Na-Na ended at a fair in Bethel, with the town asking the festival to return, despite a sea of debris left behind. The event saw 5,000 youths treated for various conditions, including drug-related issues, during the festival.

stories.headline: NIXON VISITS INDIA; HE AGAIN PRAISES REGIME IN SAIGON; Says His Talk With Thieu Disproves Speculation on a Reduced Commitment IN NEW DELHI 22 HOURS President and Mrs. Gandhi Discuss Asia and the War -- Arrives in Pakistan Nixon Visits India and Sees Mrs. Gandhi; He Again Praises Thieu Government ASIA AND THE WAR SUBJECT OF TALKS 22-Hour Stay in New Delhi -- President Is Pleased by His Flight to Saigon
stories.summary: President Nixon visited India, where he praised the government of South Vietnam and its leader Nguyen Van Thieu, expressing support for the regime during his talks with Prime Minister Gandhi. He also discussed the war in Asia with Gandhi.

stories.headline: NIXON ENDS TOUR OF ASIA WITH HOPE FOR ERA OF PEACE; Flies to Bucharest After Discussions in Pakistan on U.S. Arms Embargo TALKS TERMED CORDIAL Support of Self-Reliant Asia Is Promised During His Stopover in Lahore Nixon Ends Asian Tour and Leaves for Rumania After Voicing Hope for Peace EMBARGO ON ARMS BY U.S. DISCUSSED Talks in Lahore Described as 'Helpful' by President -- Flies to Bucharest
stories.summary: President Nixon concluded his tour of Asia, expressing hope for a new era of peace after discussions in Pakistan, where he promised support for a self-reliant Asia. He also discussed the US arms embargo with Pakistani leaders.

stories.headline: ROCKEFELLER CALLS NIXON'S PROPOSAL UNFAIR TO STATE; Contends Industrial Areas Would Be 'Shortchanged' by Welfare Reforms GOVERNOR UNSATISFIED He Sees No 'Significant' Aid for Regions Where Relief Exerts Heaviest Burden Rockefeller Charges Nixon's Proposal on Welfare Reforms Shortchanges Industrialized States
stories.summary: Governor Rockefeller criticized President Nixon's welfare reform proposal, arguing that it would unfairly shortchange industrialized states like New York, which already have high payment standards. Rockefeller claimed the plan would burden regions with high relief costs.

rounds.blurb: Woodstock Festival ended with a 19-hour concert featuring Jimi Hendrix. President Nixon visited India and Pakistan, praising the South Vietnamese government and discussing the war in Asia. He then concluded his Asian tour, expressing hope for a new era of peace.
